description: Solo entry from MIT ADT University, building an astronaut health self-assessment tool.
summary: AstraVital is a privacy-first web app that runs offline from a local copy, helping astronauts on long missions track their own health. Crew log the indicators the challenge brief names - blood pressure, heart rate, blood sugar, body temperature, sleep, and mood - plus blood oxygen and daily radiation dose. The app turns readings into color-coded status (green/yellow/red), trend charts, a clickable body-systems map, and plain-language guidance: how to measure each indicator, why it matters in space, what to re-check, and when to notify a flight surgeon. It is grounded in NASA Human Research Program's five hazards of human spaceflight, so the guidance connects each indicator to the hazard that threatens it. Mission-environment profiles (space station, transit, lunar, Mars) adapt the guidance to the comm delay and autonomy the crew actually has.
details:
What it does: AstraVital gives a crew member one daily check-in: enter eight health indicators, see each one's status at a glance, and read actionable guidance. A body map shows which body system each indicator belongs to; trend charts show how values move across the mission; a routine system prompts the next check-in and rewards consistency.

How it works: The app is a single-page web application in plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript with no dependencies, no accounts, and no network calls - important on a bandwidth-limited, delay-tolerant mission. Data lives in the browser. Each indicator is compared against reference bands; the worst indicator sets the overall crew status, and the guidance panel explains the next step in plain language, including how to take each measurement correctly.

Clinical honesty: The prototype is explicitly non-clinical: every band is labelled illustrative and cites its terrestrial source (MedlinePlus, AHA/ACC 2017, American Diabetes Association, CDC). It makes no diagnosis and no fitness-for-duty call - it shows crew what to re-check and when to escalate to a flight surgeon, mirroring real mission medical operations. Gamification rewards showing up and logging honestly, never the readings themselves, so it can never discourage reporting a symptom.

Benefits: Long missions - especially Mars transits with up to ~44 minutes of round-trip comm delay - put health assessment in the crew's hands. AstraVital supports that autonomy: structured self-checks, early trend detection, and clear escalation guidance, all running offline from a local copy.

Tools: Vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript, SVG, Canvas. No frameworks, no application backend, no transmission of readings, no cost. Verified: the code makes zero network calls, so a saved local copy runs fully offline; the public demo is a static hosted page (first load needs the network, like any website).
